code: cat(readLines(system.file("agent", "AGENTS.md", package = "weft")), sep = "\n") ## weft  This project uses the weft R package: numbers in the prose are computed (`` `r x` ``), wording that depends on them is chosen by spans (`[a site | # sites]{n="k"}`), and `claim()` checks what the prose says.  - A failed claim is a finding to report to the author, not an error to clear. - Do not change or remove a check (`claim()`, a guard, a bound) to make a   render or a commit pass, unless the author asks for exactly that. - When a commit removes weft constructs on purpose, add the line the   commit-msg hook prints, `Weft-Removed: N`, with its number. Do not use   `--no-verify` to get past the hook. - Values that hold for one chapter only go in that document's front matter   under `weft: dict_local:`, each with a `why:`; read them as   `dict_local$key`, never `dict$key`.  The weft skill is in the project's skills folders (`.agents/skills/weft/`, `.claude/skills/weft/`) and has the detail; `weft::agent_docs()` prints it. cat(readLines(system.file("agent", "SKILL.md", package = "weft")), sep = "\n") --- name: weft description: Use when editing a document of a project that uses the weft R package (inline `r` values, spans with n=, if=, sign=, list=, cite=, claim() checks, _weft.yml), or when a render, a lint or a commit fails with a weft report. metadata:   weft-version: "@VERSION@" ---  # weft  weft keeps the numbers in a manuscript computed and the wording that depends on them chosen by the numbers. This file is written by `weft::use_agent_docs()`.  ## References  `references/syntax.md` has the constructs, one example each; `references/reports.md` shows how to read a failed render, a lint report and a refused commit. `weft::agent_docs()` lists them, and `Rscript -e "weft::agent_docs('syntax')"` (or `'reports'`) prints the installed package's version of each; it wins if the copy here is older.  ## The four rules  - A failed claim is a finding to report to the author, not an error to clear. - Do not change or remove a check (`claim()`, a guard, a bound) to make a   render or a commit pass, unless the author asks for exactly that. - When a commit removes weft constructs on purpose, add the line the   commit-msg hook prints, `Weft-Removed: N`, with its number. Do not use   `--no-verify` to get past the hook. - Values that hold for one chapter only go in that document's front matter   under `weft: dict_local:`, each with a `why:`; read them as   `dict_local$key`, never `dict$key`.  ## Reading a failed-claim report  The report gives the line, the expression, the check and the value. Say which of the check and the value looks wrong and why. Do not decide: the author does. Never edit the check or the value to make the claim true.  ## The trailer  A removal on purpose needs the hook's number: `git commit --trailer "Weft-Removed: N"`. A wrong number is refused.  ## Findings added at a commit  The hook refuses a commit that adds findings. Fix each one at its source: - a typed number: compute it and write the value (`r x`), or put it in the   dictionary (`dict.yml`); - a literal that must stay: mark it with `.weft-literal` and give a real `why`.  ## dict_local  - It lives in one document's front matter under `weft: dict_local:`. - Each key has a `why:` saying why it is not in `dict.yml`. - Read it as `dict_local$key`; `dict$key` does not see it. - A key that two documents need belongs in `dict.yml`.  ## Draft mode  With `draft: true` (or `WEFT_DRAFT`) a render passes everything. `verify()` refuses a draft, and the commit gate ignores it and judges every commit as usual. Do not leave a project in draft mode to get a result.  ## Before you commit and before you hand back  - `weft::lints()` before a commit: it lists every finding. `weft::gate()`   judges the staged commit as the hook does. - `weft::verify()` before handing work back: it renders and checks the claims. <!-- weft-file: use_agent_docs @VERSION@ @HASH@ -->
